criteria.name: Post-agreement security climate
criteria.description: Assess whether overall security conditions in Tigray are stabilizing or deteriorating since the peace deal, noting persistence of unrest despite formal cessation of hostilities.

criteria.name: Factional split within ruling movement
criteria.description: Examine internal divisions within the dominant regional party, how competing factions emerged, and how the split threatens governance and peace implementation.

criteria.name: Control over armed forces
criteria.description: Evaluate the extent to which civilian leaders and party factions exert authority over regional armed formations, and how incomplete disarmament heightens risks of renewed violence.

criteria.name: Federal–regional power dynamics
criteria.description: Analyze interactions between the interim regional administration and the federal government, including appointments, oversight, and potential intervention scenarios.

criteria.name: Legal and institutional legitimacy
criteria.description: Review party registration, electoral requirements, and institutional recognition, and how procedural disputes affect claims to authority and the transition to elected governance.

criteria.name: Geographic patterns of support
criteria.description: Identify whether support for factions aligns with sub-regional or locality-based patterns and the extent to which these patterns are fluid rather than rigidly territorial.

criteria.name: Risk of intra-Tigray violence
criteria.description: Assess triggers and pathways for internal armed confrontation, including leadership targeting, factional mobilization, and clashes in disputed areas.

criteria.name: Impact on peace agreement implementation
criteria.description: Consider how internal disputes impede key provisions such as disarmament, reintegration, territorial arrangements, and the establishment of a regional government through elections.

criteria.name: Spillover from neighboring conflicts
criteria.description: Evaluate how concurrent unrest in adjacent regions and disputed territories influences security dynamics and escalatory risks in Tigray.

criteria.name: Humanitarian and displacement context
criteria.description: Assess how lingering displacement and slow recovery from prior war amplify the costs of renewed instability and complicate reconciliation.

criteria.name: Mediation and dialogue efforts
criteria.description: Examine the role and effectiveness of civil society, religious leaders, and international partners in facilitating dialogue and preventing escalation.

criteria.name: Public sentiment and legitimacy crisis
criteria.description: Gauge local perceptions of factional motives, trust in leadership, and calls for alternative political options, and how these views affect stability.

criteria.name: Scenarios and outlook
criteria.description: Outline plausible near-term outcomes—consolidation by one faction or escalation to violence—and their implications for governance and civilian security.

criteria.name: Security incidents post-ceasefire
criteria.description: Track patterns of armed incidents involving regional forces or militias since the ceasefire, focusing on whether incidents are isolated or indicative of systematic relapse.

criteria.name: Administrative control maneuvers
criteria.description: Monitor attempts by factions to seize or retain control of interim government positions and party organs, and their compliance with procedural rules.
